patients.summary: IT specialist who joined in 2021 healthy apart from a mild chronic anemia. Develops sarcoidosis with erythema nodosum (2023), primary adrenal insufficiency on replacement (2024), and in 2025 necrolytic migratory erythema that leads to a glucagonoma of the pancreatic tail, resected with splenectomy in December 2025.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
43M here to establish. Transferring from another primary care office; records requested. Works in IT, mostly desk work. Feels well. No meds, no supplements. NKDA.

PMH: nothing chronic that he knows of.
PSH: appendectomy at 16, no complications.
FH: father with type 2 diabetes. Mother with autoimmune thyroiditis. One sister with pulmonary sarcoidosis, doing OK.
SH: married, lives in Easthampton. Never smoked. Drinks socially, a beer or two a week. No formal exercise.

ROS negative across the board: no chest pain, SOB, cough, GI or GU complaints, no weight change, sleeping fine.

Exam: well appearing. BP and HR as recorded. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or nodules. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ scar. Skin without rash. Ext no edema. Mood and affect normal.

COVID: two Pfizer doses this spring at a pharmacy (card seen). Last tetanus he can't recall -> Tdap today.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c (father with DM), TSH (mother's thyroid), one-time HIV and hep C screens. Colon screening discussed, he'll be due at 45. Flu shot in the fall.
2. Diet/activity: brief counseling, aim for 150 min/wk.

RTC 1 yr for physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: MA Intake
documents.author: MA
documents.body: New pt intake. Vitals obtained. Med list reviewed: none. Allergies: NKDA, confirmed. PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2. Pt brought COVID card, 2 doses entered as historical. Release of information signed for prior PCP office.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jamal, your labs look good overall: kidney and liver tests, sugar (A1c), cholesterol and thyroid are all normal, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Your hemoglobin is a touch low at 12.4, with normal-sized red cells. That isn't anything to act on right now, but I'd like to recheck it at your physical next year. Let me know if you ever notice unusual tiredness, shortness of breath, or dark stools before then.

documents.title: RE: Your recent labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks doc. Sounds good, I'll get the physical on the calendar.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received 14 pages by fax from patient's former primary care office (records dated 2012 through 2020). Scanned to chart.

Summary for provider: yearly physicals, last 2020-02. Problem list blank. Surgical hx appendectomy as a teenager. No medications. Allergies none recorded. Lipids and glucose normal on file. Flu shots most years. No specialist referrals.

Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior records. Nothing new. Agree with summary.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal flu vaccine. Feels well today, no fever. No prior vaccine reactions. VIS given. Influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Tolerated, waited 15 min without issue.

documents.title: Employer wellness form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my employer's insurance wants a biometric screening form filled out for the wellness discount. Can I use my labs from August or do I need to come in? Form attached.

documents.title: RE: Employer wellness form
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mr. Robinson, the doctor filled in the form with your August values and it's uploaded to your portal documents. Your physical is due in August and we can book that now if you like.

documents.title: RE: Employer wellness form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Perfect. Mid August, mornings are best.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Doing well. Busy year at work. Sleeping 7 h. No fatigue he'd call out of the ordinary. No bleeding, no dark or bloody stools, eats meat a few times a week. No NSAID use.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: NAD. Vitals reviewed. Conjunctivae pink. Neck no LAD, thyroid normal. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abd soft, NT, no HSM. Skin clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Hgb 12.4 last year, normocytic. Repeat CBC w/ diff today plus iron studies, B12, folate.
2. Preventive: CMP, lipids, A1c. Flu shot this fall + updated COVID booster when available. Colonoscopy next year at 45.

RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.9, MCV 83, rest of the CBC unremarkable. Iron, ferritin, B12 and folate all normal. Second mildly low value a year apart with nothing to chase on iron or vitamins. Will carry as chronic mild normocytic anemia and trend yearly. CMP, lipids, A1c normal. Messaged pt.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count is still mildly low (hemoglobin 11.9) but your iron, B12 and folate levels are all normal, so there's no deficiency to treat. I've added it to your problem list as a mild long-standing anemia, and we'll keep an eye on it every year. Everything else, including cholesterol and sugar, is normal.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu + bivalent COVID booster. Afebrile, feels well. Screening questions negative. Flu vaccine R deltoid, Pfizer bivalent L deltoid. VIS/EUA fact sheet given. No reaction during 15 min observation. Pt aware sore arm/low grade temp possible for a day.
